question: Can I install the command-line tool as a regular project package instead of system-wide? Do I need to change any config files for it to use the local version, or does it figure it out automatically?
ground_truth: To install Fern CLI as a local project dependency, run `npm install fern-api` to add it to your package.json, ensuring version consistency across your team. You do need to update your `fern.config.json` file - set the `version` field to `"*"` to tell Fern to use your locally installed version instead of downloading a specific global version. Then run Fern commands through your package manager by prefixing with `npm`: `npm fern check`, `npm fern --version`, `npm fern generate`, etc. This approach solves both problems: it works in restricted CI environments (since the package is installed via npm in package.json) and ensures all developers use the exact same CLI version tracked in version control. The local installation won't auto-detect without the version: "*" change in fern.config.json - this configuration tells Fern to use the local node_modules version.

metadata.cited_context:
If you're experiencing network delays with the global installation, working in an environment with limited internet connectivity, or prefer to manage Fern as a project dependency, you can install the CLI locally:

Add `fern-api` to your project dependencies:

```bash
npm install fern-api
```

In your `fern.config.json`, set the version to `*` to use your locally installed version:

```json fern.config.json
{
  "organization": "your-org",
  "version": "*"
}
```

Use your package manager to run Fern commands:

```bash
npm fern check        # Validate API definition
npm fern --version    # Check CLI version
npm fern generate     # Generate outputs
```
